steps.text: Whisk Italian dressing, Worcestershire sauce, applesauce, hot pepper sauce, and lime juice together in a large glass or ceramic bowl. Add pork chops and toss to evenly coat. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap; marinate in the refrigerator for 6 hours or overnight.
Preheat an outdoor grill for medium heat and lightly oil the grate.
Remove chops from marinade and shake off excess. Pour marinade into a saucepan and bring to a boil over medium heat. Boil for about 1 minute; set aside.

Cook pork chops on the preheated grill until well browned and no longer pink in the center, about 6 minutes per side; occasionally basting chops with marinade until basted marinade cooks completely onto chops. An instant-read thermometer inserted into centers should read 145 degrees F (63 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Bada Bing Pork Chops
raw_recipe.description: Bada bing pork chops start with marinating chops in a savory, sweet Italian dressing, hot sauce, applesauce, and lime juice mixture before grilling.

video.description: Up the ante on your pork chop flavor with this awesome and easy grilled recipe! First create a zesty marinade with Italian dressing, Worcestershire sauce, applesauce, hot pepper sauce and a bright splash of lime juice. Marinate your chops overnight, then grill them up juicy with tempting crispy-browned edges, and baste them with the marinade for the full bada bing! flavor everyone enjoys!

review.reviewBody: I have made these 2 times and each time they received rave reviews. I do recommend marinating overnight for maximum flavor. Great recipe!

I used 1/2 " boneless chops, browned and then slow simmered in the sauce. I used Mott's applesauce with cinnamon and less Worcestershire. I used light Italian dressing and Franks hot sauce to taste.
1/4 cup or so. Simmered the chops on low for about 1 1/2 hours instead of grilling. Served with fresh Country green beans (recipe on All recipes too) and roasted red skin potatoes. Used the extra sauce for dipping Texas toast in. Husband and 16 year old son loved it! Said it was "nice restaurant quality"!

OMG-- These are fantastic. Strange ingredients worked GREAT together. I left out the hot sauce and used lemon juice instead of lime and added a bit of rosemary. I marinated overnight and braised them on the stove with the marinade which cooked down into a delicious gravy. Definitely a keeper.

Wow! That's all I can say! I did a quick 30 minute marinade on this cuz I was in a pinch. Cooked em on the stove with a grill pan! Seared the chops then added about 1/4 of the marinade and cooked it with the chops bout 7 mins per side. Let stand 4 mins and topped the chops with the drippings. 3 letters. OMG. Doing this one again.

This recipe also works well in the crock pot. The tangy juice is so yummy over rice. We loved it and I imagine they are even more amazing on the grill. The ingredients were just perfect for us and I only added a small amount of water to the crock pot to make the juice very flavorful. Thank you!!!

I used sliced pork tenderloin (about 2" thick) medallions and let them thaw in the marinade for 2 days. I had a schedule conflict and could not grill, so we put all of it, plus about 6 red potatoes in the slow cooker on high for 5 hours. I drained the marinade out, boiled it with cornstarch and turned it into a gravy. It was good, a bit spicy, and we look forward to trying it on the gril.
We really liked this dish. I added 1/4 cup of sweet chili sauce and baked it in the oven at 425 for an hour. Nice and easy.

WOW! I am not one for hot (spicy) food, but these were amazing! When I was preparing the marinade, I thought for sure I was not going to like them due to the large amount of pepper sauce. Yes, there was tingling, but it wasn't bad. I would recommend a longer marinating time with thicker chops. Putting the marinade on during the grilling process extremely enhanced the flavor & created some nice crispy ends! Definitely will make again!!

Decided to give this one a try on the ol' George Foreman, and SUCCESS! Huge fan of simple recipes, and it doesn't get much easier. Of course, that doesn't matter if it isn't tasty...double win. Instead of bone-in chops, I opted for a thinner, center cut, boneless chop. Cooked for about 4 minutes on medium, and it worked great. Will probably cook a little hotter next time to get some char. Marinating overnight is highly recommended. I still cooked the marinade to thicken, and gave the meat a good, final dunk before cooking. This is a tasty, easy entree. Whip it together the night before, throw it on the portable grill when you get home the next day. Dinner in minutes!
Really good. I broiled it which produced some smoke, but all was well. Used soy sauce instead of Worcestershire. Husband approved.
We had a menu change so ended up marinating these for a day and a half. I baked them in the marinade, covered, for 30 minutes at 350 degrees. Very flavorful and juicy.
Great combination of flavors. Gotta plan ahead to marinate; poke the chops with a fork to let the goodness in before refrigerating. Left out the hot sauce because we don't like it.
These were a big hit! The marinade is excellent! Since the grill was on, I put on split chicken breasts and baby back pork ribs and used the marinade- BADA BING for sure!!!!
they were delish!

I made the recipe as stated. It turned out just fine. I do not have any qualms with the recipe itself; however, I just wasn't that thrilled with the overall taste. It wasn't bad, but it didn't knock my socks off. I have other recipes for pork chops that I prefer more. Just a personal preference is all. I may, at some point, try this with chicken instead. I think I might prefer it more with a different protein.
Really good marinade, was great with both pork and chicken.
keeper, will make again

I made this for Sunday dinner. I did not have hot sauce and Worcestershire sauce. I substituted the hot sauce for barbecue sauce. The meat was flavorful and tender. The next time I will make sure to have Worcestershire sauce.

Used Siracha as the hot sauce. Only let it marinate about 3 hours. Worked great. The sauce was spicy enough that I was concerned my wife wouldn't like it, but with the meat, it was perfect. Just a bit of heat, but not overwhelming.
Fabulous grill-centered dish. Makes a hero out of Dad
